accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:joint-system-limit and thm:separate-joint-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Optimality is confined to constant loadings in the fixed retained vector of pairwise DDD scores; it is not the semiparametric efficiency bound of the full conditional-moment DDD model.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The accepted field claim is feasible joint score-span GMM inference and its joint-versus-componentwise frontier for fixed T, retained comparisons, and prespecified aggregate weights.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies each ATT(g,t) with every admissible clean comparison cohort and gives the covariance-optimal GMM combination separately within that ATT(g,t) block.

The paper derives a fixed-weight stacked event-study CLT, includes shared comparison-unit covariance, and estimates variance by summing original-unit influence contributions before squaring; it presents stacked DDD as complementary to GMM.

The paper derives closed-form semiparametric efficient influence functions and estimators for overidentified staggered DiD and event-study parameters using conditional covariance weighting, not an eligibility-domain DDD system.
The paper derives canonical panel-DDD identification, efficient influence-function estimators, and cross-fitting, but does not treat staggered clean-comparison overidentification.

The DML theory uses cross-fitting, moment-envelope control, nuisance-quality conditions, and orthogonality to derive asymptotic linearity; the proposal supplies score-specific sufficient L4 and product-rate conditions rather than attributing its calculation to the generic theorem.
The paper establishes large-sample GMM theory and covariance-optimal weighting for overidentified unconditional moments, but not the DDD score construction or cross-block frontier.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Derive the conditional-moment semiparametric efficient influence function for staggered DDD and compare its attainable bound directly with both the proposed constant-score-span loading and ChenSantAnnaXie2025.

Resolve the open construction with a bounded positive-definite three-score law, then prove that strict gain holds on an open nondegenerate compatible-covariance region rather than only at one worked law.
Add a practical diagnostic corollary giving a consistent test or confidence interval for the estimated quadratic efficiency-loss functional.

recommended_next_step: Advance this field-tier proposal to Stage 0, retaining the fixed score-span limitation as the settled scope boundary.
